title: Théorie arithmétique. Théorie de Galois des motifs (1965) : notes manuscites (s.d.), tapuscrit (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page carries no new writing of its own. It is the show-through of the following sheet: the faint line layout, the underlined 'Définition', 'Scolie', the displayed 'τλ = λ̄' and 'τ² = 1', and the last lines about 'la plus grande extension abélienne A de K' all match the next page line by line. The content is therefore that of the next page.

(1) Definition. An algebraic extension K/Q is totally real if σ(K) ⊂ R for every Q-embedding σ: K → C. An element x is totally real, totally > 0 or totally ≥ 0 if every σ(x) is real, > 0 or ≥ 0 respectively.

(2) Scolie (elementary facts):
- x is totally real iff Q(x) is.
- x is totally ≥ 0 iff x = 0 or x is totally > 0.
- 'Totally ≥' defines a (partial) order on K.
- A compositum of totally real fields is totally real.
- Hence K has a largest totally real subfield.

(3) Galois side. Fix Q̄ ⊂ C, let π = Gal(Q̄/Q) and let τ be complex conjugation, with τ² = 1. The maximal totally real subfield Q^{tr} of Q̄ corresponds to π', the closed normal subgroup generated by τ, i.e. by its conjugates στσ⁻¹. The text then considers the maximal abelian extension A of Q^{tr}, with group π'/[π',π'].

Purpose in the dossier 'Théorie de Galois des motifs': this is set-up for the role of complex conjugation and totally real / CM fields. These matter for polarizations, positivity, Weil numbers and the motivic Galois group of CM-type motives (compare Serre's and Langlands' Taniyama group). The preceding page in the scan is unrelated: a typed translation of a Russian paper on projective embeddings, misfiled.
